text: The book stresses that when Physarum 'solves' a maze with food at the entrance and exit, it does NOT do so by searching. What actually produces the shortest-path solution?
choices: The plasmodium evaluates each candidate path, holds them in memory, and selects the best one
Individual nuclei vote on the preferred route by migrating toward it
A central pacemaker region computes the optimal path and directs tube growth
The plasmodium first occupies all paths, then flow reinforcement thickens high-flow tubes and prunes low-flow ones
explanation: Physarum spreads through the whole maze and then flow reinforcement (governed by Hagen-Poiseuille dynamics) thickens tubes carrying more flow while draining those carrying less, so the shortest path is selected by competitive self-organization. There is no search, no stored comparison of paths (choice 0), no nuclear voting (choice 1), and crucially no command center or pacemaker (choice 2) in the plasmodium.
